items.title: Verstappen wins a slipstream thriller from Norris and Piastri
items.summary: Verstappen led from pole and held off a race-long Mercedes challenge to win ahead of the McLaren pair (Norris +0.639s, Piastri +1.529s on The Race's result). Mercedes dropped back late: Russell made a mistake and crashed, and Antonelli finished fourth after a last-lap issue.
items.why_it_matters: The slipstream produced more than 20 lead changes (The Race) and the winner was decided in the final laps, so treat this as a venue-specific race, not a template for Qatar.

items.title: Hamilton and Leclerc collide again; Vasseur calls it unacceptable
items.summary: The Ferrari drivers tangled in Las Vegas, two races after their first-lap clash in Mexico. Vasseur called it 'a lack of respect' and 'unacceptable'; Leclerc said he would accept the blame and was embarrassed; Hamilton called his penalty 'really harsh'. The Race lists Ferrari as 7th and 10th.
items.why_it_matters: It is a repeat management problem for Ferrari going into the final two rounds and a question to put to both drivers in Qatar.

items.title: Perez takes a five-place grid penalty in Qatar after the Camara collision
items.summary: Perez attempted to pass Haas' Rafael Camara approaching Turn 14; the Cadillac's front right touched Camara's rear left and both ended up in trouble. Formula1.com reports a five-place grid penalty for the next race, Qatar.
items.why_it_matters: It is the first confirmed Qatar grid sanction; check the final classification and any further stewards' documents before quoting the starting order.

items.title: Hadjar's front wing failure and post-race demotion
items.summary: Hadjar, who started fourth and featured in the early lead battle, lost his front wing and said he was still waiting for the team to explain it. A post-race penalty also demoted him one place.
items.why_it_matters: The cause is unconfirmed; do not describe it as a design or reliability fault until Red Bull says so.
